questions.prompt: What does scores > 85 evaluate to when scores is an array?
choices: An array of True and False, one per element
questions.explain: Elementwise, like every other numpy operation. That array of answers is what does the selecting.

questions.prompt: How do you write "over 70 and under 90" as a mask?
questions.explain: Python's `and` needs one truth value per side and an array refuses to give one. The brackets matter because & binds tighter than the comparisons.
True counts as 1, so summing a boolean array counts the matches without selecting anything.

choices: Sets every element over 100 to 100, in place
questions.explain: A mask works on the left of an assignment too. Note "in place" — the array you were handed is the one that changed.
